text: ANSWERED, after an extra call. Singapore CPI All Items was 100.661 in Dec 2024 on the 2024=100 base. Periods came back as 2024-12, so the SingStat normalisation claim holds.

FINDING, and this one is decisive. The fetch returned 15 series keyed SERIES 1, 1.0, 1.01, 1.01.1 and so on, which are hierarchy positions with no names. Asking search_codes for the same dimension returns {id: 1, name: All Items, unit: Index}. The labels exist, the fetch path already looks up codelists to resolve units, and it still hands back bare codes. An agent cannot tell which of 15 numbered series is the headline CPI without a second round trip it has no reason to know it needs.

FINDING: with limit=15 over an unfiltered key the budget split 15 series one observation each, so a request for a year of CPI returned one month of 15 sub-indices. The split is working as designed; the problem is that narrowing to one series requires a code the response does not name.
FIXED. names now gives SERIES 1 All Items, 1.0 Food, 1.01.1 Rice & Cereal Products. The headline CPI is identifiable from the response.
